recommendation.answer: Concrete fix: Deploy Strict CSP with script-src 'nonce-{RANDOM}' 'strict-dynamic'. Nonces are unique one-time-use random values generated for each HTTP response. 'strict-dynamic' trusts those elements without explicitly adding nonces or hashes. When inline scripts are required, script-src hash allows only specific scripts. Preventing the page from executing inline scripts mitigates injecting <script>.

sources.contribution: 'strict-dynamic' tells the browser to trust those elements as well without having to explicitly add nonces or hashes for each one
When inline scripts are required, the script-src 'hash_algo-hash' is another option for allowing only specific scripts to execute
By preventing the page from executing inline scripts, attacks like injecting < script > document

fix.summary: Deploy per-response nonce CSP with strict-dynamic and inject nonce into all script tags so inline and external scripts stay trusted without unsafe-inline.
fix.risk: If a proxy caches HTML with old nonce or a script tag uses uppercase SCRIPT it could be blocked; fetch journeys unaffected.
